newsitem.title: UK: Lib Dems want tax on perks to fund better NHS.
newsitem.headline: Lib Dems want tax on perks to fund better NHS.

text.p: Closing a tax loophole that encourages bankers and brokers to receive their bonuses in perks instead of pay could raise 350 million stg to improve health care, the Liberal Democrats said on Wednesday.

Health spokesman Simon Hughes told his party's annual conference that firms were avoiding paying national insurance contributions when they substituted gifts in kind to well-paid executives for normal salary.
"Millions of pounds have been paid in gold bars, life (insurance) policies and other valuables to avoid paying tax to the Exchequer," he told delegates.
"Responsible firms shouldn't spend their time thinking up tax wheezes and we wouldn't let them."
Bonuses of tens or even hundreds of thousands of pounds are not uncommon in the City of London.
Hughes said closing the loophole by insisting bonuses are paid in cash could bring in 350 million pounds a year, which the party proposed should be earmarked to ease the pressure on the creaking NHS.
It could be used to employ more than 10,000 extra NHS nurses and to cut waiting times for hospital operations.
Later David Laws, a parliamentary researcher for the Liberals, said the Treasury had now closed the gold bars tax loophole.

But he said this has merely prompted the firms to find new ways round the tax -- for instance by offering valued employees cases of fine wine, insurance policies that they promptly cashed in or loans at artificially low interest rates.
Hughes also detailed a plan to raise tax on cigarettes by five pence per packet of 20 to fund a scheme to give all Britons the right to free check-ups by opticians and dentists.
